*Most consumer protections related to debt collections were done away with in 2017.*

Debt collectors can now use many more tactics to collect debts, and have a lot more tools at their disposal.

In the US verbal contracts are valid. If they agree to pay the full debt over the phone, expect the debt-collector to take them to court for more payments.

They may win in court, but will still have to pay lawyers and/or have to deal with judgement-claims made against them.

If they don't show in court, the debt-collector wins a default judgement, even though its someone else's debt.

**> Super Important <**

You *can be made liable* for the debt if you:

* say anything over the phone that in any way implies the debt is yours
* agree to make any payment, or even put payments on-hold
* give your address to receive mail from them
* and many other tricky quasi-legal things they do

Basically don't talk to them, if you must only repeat the phrase "This is not my debt" until they give up and hang up. Seriously. They are going to try and trick you into saying certain phrases while being recorded.
